lines.text: Stores love Black Friday, but the name came from cops who dreaded it.
You see, in Philadelphia, the day after Thanksgiving was the worst day of the year to be a traffic cop.
Shoppers packed downtown, and fans poured in for the Army-Navy football game.
No traffic cop was allowed to take the day off. They even ordered the police band downtown.
So the cops called it Black Friday.
The city wanted a nicer name, so a PR expert suggested one.
Nobody used it. The reporters kept writing Black Friday.
For twenty years, it stayed mostly a Philadelphia thing, about traffic.
Then, in 1981, a better story showed up in print.
It said Black Friday is the day stores finally go from red ink to black, from losses to profit.
You see, that was the version stores loved, and it spread across the country.
In 1985, store owners in [Los Angeles](/lɔs ˈænʤələs/) and Cincinnati still hadn't heard of it.
So the profit story isn't where the name came from. It's the rebrand that finally worked.
And this November twenty-seventh, while you shop, remember. The name was invented by cops stuck in traffic.
